nightly-bot: [ALERT] nightly-eval job 2026-03-19T04:12Z — 27/200 prompts failed for model redwood-v2-q4_0. Failure class: fncall JSON parse errors (schema mismatch). Job: https://redwood.internal/evals/2026-03-19/789 :eyes:
sara: I pulled a few failing examples. The model emitted the tool call payload but several fields are wrong type. Example output from the model:```json
{"tool":"fetch_items","args":"{\"ids\":\"W10K\",\"limit\":\"5\",\"meta\":\"{\\\"len\\\":\\\"3\\\"}\"}"}
```Note: args is a string (double-encoded) and inside that, ids is base64-ish string instead of an array. Also meta.len is a string instead of int. This causes our strict JSON schema checker to raise parse/type errors. :thinking_face:
mike: Which runner + quantization level? Is this happening only on q4_0? Any repro locally?
raj: Confirmed it's redwood-v2-q4_0 running on dedicated-quant pool. We've seen the kernel path that serializes small arrays into compact tokens when the KV cache hits a certain pattern. That path accidentally stringifies nested arrays when using the legacy tokenizer postprocess.
eva: Two options: 1) Make the eval harness tolerant (try json.loads on stringified args then coerce types), or 2) Treat these as real regressions and block the model until the runtime fix lands. I lean to tagging as "schema-coercion" so we can track frequency without masking issues.
sara: Quick local repro command (uses nightly runner image):
```
./tools/run_eval --model redwood-v2-q4_0 --prompts tests/edge-toolcall-set.json --job tmp/repro-789
cat tmp/repro-789/out.ndjson | jq '.[] | select(.error!=null)'
```
Output snippet after repro:```json
{"prompt_id":"p117","model_out":{"tool":"fetch_items","args":"{\"ids\":\"W10K\",\"limit\":\"5\"}"},"error":"schema: args not object"}
```Re-ran with runtime build sha abc1234 (contains the small kernel fix raj mentioned) and the same prompt now yields:
```json
{"prompt_id":"p117","model_out":{"tool":"fetch_items","args":{"ids":[123,456,789],"limit":5}},"error":null}
```
So the kernel fix seems to address the double-encoding in this case. :+1:
mike: Good. Let's not auto-coerce in harness for now — we risk hiding regressions — but we should add a non-blocking label as eva suggested and surface counts in the nightly dashboard. Can someone open a follow-up ticket to track schema-coercion failures vs hard parse failures?
raj: Created ticket RW-ENG-4212: "Track schema-coercion failures from nightly evals" and a small PR with a safe_json_parse util: https://redwood.internal/pulls/2314 — it adds logging and a non-blocking flag when args are stringified and recoverable.
eva: I'll add dashboard tile and an alert that fires only if coercion count spikes >5% of failures in a day.
sara: Thanks — I'll run a full nightly re-run for the affected prompt set and attach updated artifacts to RW-ENG-4212. For now marking this incident as "triaged (kernel fix landed, monitoring added)". :white_check_mark:
